# requireNaN

<link-summary>Returns the value as `NaN`, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNaN() — Returns the value as `NaN`, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/number</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNaN(value: unknown, message: string = "Expected NaN."): number;
```

Nothing is coerced first, which is where this differs from the global `isNaN`: that one converts its argument, so `isNaN("abc")` and `isNaN(undefined)` both report `true`.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                  | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :----------------------------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                    | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected NaN."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`number` — the same value, typed as `NaN`.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                          |
| :------------------------- | :--------------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not the `NaN` number. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNaN(NaN); // => NaN
requireNaN(0 / 0); // => 0 / 0
requireNaN(0); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNaN("abc"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
